title: Mind the Gap: Evaluating the Representativeness of Quantitative Medical Language Reasoning LLM Benchmarks for African Disease Burdens

bias_targets.methodology: Quantitative semantic profiling using Named Entity Recognition (NER) to count mentions of Neglected Tropical Diseases (NTDs) and specific high-burden African diseases (e.g., malaria, HIV, TB, sickle-cell disease) across medical QA benchmarks, comparing their representation against high-income clinical contexts.

Blinded expert qualitative rating of benchmark questions on a five-point Likert scale to evaluate 'Language and Cultural Appropriateness,' assessing how well the questions respect local context, patient diversity, and African traditions versus Western generalized clinical scenarios.

Quantitative semantic analysis evaluating text readability (Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level), sentence length, and lexical diversity (TTR, MTLD, HDD), combined with expert reviews on clarity, cognitive load, and the lack of multilingual support (e.g., English-only focus) for African healthcare workers.
